stem.text: Let \( f(x) = -\left(\sqrt[5]{x - 1}\right)^{4} - 2 \). Determine whether f is differentiable at \( x = 1 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is not differentiable at \( x = 1 \), because the difference quotient grows without bound with opposite signs on the two sides, so the graph has a cusp there.

worked_solution.text: f is continuous at \( x = 1 \), since \( f(1) = -2 \) and the root is continuous everywhere.
The difference quotient is \( \frac{f(1 + h) - f(1)}{h} = -h^{- \frac{1}{5}} \), and the exponent \( - \frac{1}{5} \) is negative.
Because the power of h has an odd numerator, the quotient has opposite signs for h < 0 and h > 0, and its size grows without bound as h approaches 0.
worked_solution.rule_named: one sided limits of the difference quotient

worked_solution.text: The difference quotient has no finite limit, so f is not differentiable at \( x = 1 \), and the graph has a cusp there.
